issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Meal differs between artifacts. The problem statement UML and the solution repository declare the constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (problem_statement.md shows +Meal(String, String[]) and solution/src/.../Meal.java defines public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients)). However, the template repository's Meal.java defines the constructor with reversed parameters: public Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (template/src/.../Meal.java). The template's Main.java example (commented) uses new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...}) which matches the UML/solution but will not compile against the template constructor. This mismatch will confuse students and can cause compilation or usage errors when they run or adapt the provided example.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the problem statement and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Update the constructor body to assign this.name = name and this.ingredients = ingredients accordingly. Also ensure example usages (e.g., the commented code in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) are consistent with this parameter order.
